title: Retry failed webhook deliveries with exponential backoff
summary:
This PR adds automatic retries for webhook deliveries that fail with a 5xx status or a timeout. `deliverWebhook` now records each failed attempt in a new `webhook_retries` table. A new `retryWorker` job sends due retries again, up to 6 attempts.

Before this change, one failed request dropped the event. Customers then had to poll `/events` to recover. The PR also renames `http.ts` to `http-client.ts` and deletes the unused `legacy-sender.ts`.

changes.what: `deliverWebhook` now catches 5xx responses and timeouts and calls `scheduleRetry` with the attempt count. A new `computeBackoff(attempt)` returns the delay: 30 seconds doubled per attempt, capped at 1 hour.
changes.why: This is the core behavior change. Failed deliveries are no longer dropped. Every caller of `deliverWebhook` now gets retries without code changes.

changes.what: Adds `scheduleRetry(event, attempt)`, which inserts a row into `webhook_retries` with a `run_at` time from `computeBackoff`.
changes.why: Storing retries in the database keeps them across deploys and restarts.

changes.what: Adds `retryWorker`, a job that runs every 30 seconds. It selects up to 100 due rows, calls `deliverWebhook` for each, and deletes the row on success.
changes.why: This job is the only code that sends retries, so its batch size and locking decide retry throughput.

changes.what: Creates the `webhook_retries` table with an index on `run_at`.
changes.why: The worker query filters on `run_at`, so the index keeps the poll fast as the table grows.

changes.what: Renames the file and changes the default request timeout from 30 seconds to 10 seconds.
changes.why: A shorter timeout frees workers sooner. It also counts more slow endpoints as failures, which now trigger retries.

changes.what: Deletes `sendLegacyWebhook`, which had no remaining callers.
changes.why: Removes dead code. Nothing in the repository imports it.

flow.caption: `deliverWebhook` now hands failed deliveries to `scheduleRetry`, which stores them in the `webhook_retries` table. The `retryWorker` job reads due rows and calls `deliverWebhook` again.

risks.title: Docs still describe the old 30 second timeout
risks.reason: `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` is now 10000, but `docs/webhooks.md` still says requests time out after 30 seconds.

risks.title: Two workers can send the same retry twice
risks.reason: The query selects due rows without `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`. When two `retryWorker` instances poll at the same time, both read the same rows and call `deliverWebhook` for each one. Customers receive duplicate events.

risks.title: Retries continue after the maximum attempt count
risks.reason: The check `attempt > MAX_ATTEMPTS` runs after `scheduleRetry`, so attempt 6 still schedules attempt 7. Endpoints that are down permanently get one extra request per event.

tests.description: Run two `retryWorker` processes against one database and confirm each due row is delivered once.
Point a webhook at an endpoint that returns 503 and confirm retries happen at 30s, 60s, 120s, and stop after attempt 6.
Confirm that a 4xx response does not schedule a retry.
Run the migration on a copy of production data and check that the `run_at` index exists.
Search the codebase for imports of `src/lib/http` to confirm nothing still uses the old path.
